item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Fighting has resumed in the Kherson region after the longest ceasefire ended, and Russian drones struck a Ukrainian railway station, killing 13. Russia has begun using makeshift armor of nets and rubber tires on its shadow fleet drones and adapting decoy drones for one-way attacks up to 1,200 km, while Ukrainian hackers and Russian actors have both compromised emergency alert apps, issuing fake nuclear warnings. A Russian Su‑57 fighter was destroyed by an engine fire at Akhtubinsk airfield, and Russian forces have exploited the Oleshky ceasefire to mask troop movements. The conflict caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:
Israel continues airstrikes on southern Lebanese towns such as Aita al-Jabal, Zawtar al-Sharqiyah and the Marjayoun Plain, while Hezbollah artillery fires back at Israeli positions. Hezbollah has begun distributing aid, announcing its first payment to war victims and displaced families and pledging further assistance to those uprooted by the conflict. The United Nations reports 300,000 people displaced in Lebanon due to the fighting. Damage assessments note that Israeli shelling has affected roughly a quarter of Lebanon's agricultural land, worsening the humanitarian situation.

item.title: Sudan's civil war: the situation
item.description:
Drone strikes by the RSF have hit multiple power stations across Sudan, including two in the east, causing widespread blackouts and prompting Sudan to lodge complaints with the UN and African Union against Ethiopia for cross-border attacks. The RSF continues to target civilian infrastructure, while the Sudanese army reports defections of RSF members in Blue Nile state and claims it is recruiting fighters from northern Somalia. The Sudanese government accuses Ethiopia of backing the drone attacks, and the UN is preparing talks with the RSF on a civilian transition. 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Ethiopia: the situation
item.description:
Violence in northern Ethiopia continues to push the health system toward collapse as WHO warns the system is near failure, while renewed drone strikes hit Sudan, an Amhara displacement camp and civilians gathering grain in Tigray. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has sent senior ministers to military training in Hurso and Ethiopia is accused of using Assosa Airport as a launch base for RSF drones and supplying arms to the RSF. An RPG fired near a school in Moyale killed 60 Ethiopian Orthodox believers, prompting the Orthodox Church to demand action. The conflict has displaced 1.7 million Ethiopians and affected an additional 173,000 people, according to UNHCR, and there were 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Mawisley militias have pulled back from central front lines, whereas Puntland mercenaries are fighting alongside Sudanese RSF forces, and Sudan’s army reports northern Somali fighters supporting the RSF. Somali pirates seized an Iranian fishing vessel, rescuing seven Pakistani crew members. The conflict caused 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
